citations.F1: N+1: one `users` fetchrow per event, awaited sequentially, is ~1,000 round trips per request
citations.F2: Dedupe uses a list for `seen`, so it's O(n²) per request
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` calls blocking `requests.get` (2 s timeout) inside the async handler ... freezing the event loop for the whole worker; switch to `httpx.AsyncClient`
citations.F4: no index on `(org_id, created_at)`, so every call seq-scans 4.2M rows; `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` grows forever ... replace with a bounded `deque(maxlen=...)` or a proper histogram
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is unbounded and per worker, so every unique client IP ever seen is held 4× per pod; replace with a size-capped TTL cache
citations.F7: Verify the fix under load: acme p95 under 0.5 s in Datadog, `/healthz` answers during a 1,000-event request
citations.F8: is ~1,000 round trips per request and most of the gap between the 1.4 s query and the 6 s p50
citations.F9: Do not ship the proposal: 16 workers × 50 conns × 6 pods = 4,800 Postgres connections ... Revisit caching only after 3 to 9 land and only if the numbers still demand it
citations.F10: Confirm the leak split before closing: expose `len(_geo_cache)` and `len(_request_timings)` temporarily, or run tracemalloc on one pod
citations.F11: the Redis key includes `since`, which for the mobile client is `now() - 30d` at microsecond precision, so it would never hit
